newsitem.title: FINLAND: Kesko sees EU approval of Tuko deal with changes.
newsitem.headline: Kesko sees EU approval of Tuko deal with changes.

text.p: Finnish wholesaler and retailer Kesko Oy CEO Eero Kinnunen said on Wednesday he expects the European Commission to approve its proposed acquisition of rival wholesaler Tuko, but will ask for certain changes.
Asked by telephone whether he thought the commission might reject the deal, Kinnunen said,"There are no hints whatsoever to that direction."
Kesko said earlier that the EU commission regarded the proposed acquisition as "inappropriate in the EU's merger legislation."
Kinnunen said Kesko may have to change its proposal to get the commission's approval.
"Obviously there will be some changes. I have a feeling that these will concern the relation between us and the shopkeepers," he said.

Kinnunen said the commission feared that Kesko could get a dominant market position as it regards Kesko as a chain store. However, Kesko regards itself as a wholesaler and a supplier catering to independent shopkeepers in the K-group.
"They look at us as if we were a chain store, but this is a group of independent, voluntary shopkeepers," he said.
Kesko has three weeks to supply the commission with more information, and the commission will take its final decision by November 27, Kinnunen said.
Kesko bought a majority in rival wholesaler Tuko late in May.
